newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo wants to work with U.N. probe.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo wants to work with U.N. probe.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's Congo said on Thursday that it wanted its experts to work alongside a U.N. team probing allegations that his forces or their Tutsi allies massacred Rwandan Hutu refugees.

But it acknowledged that they could not be present when the investigators, prevented from starting on time by a dispute with Kabila's government over membership of the team, interviewed potential witnesses.
"The principle is accepted, they must do their work, but they must work with us," Justice Minister Mwenze Kongolo told a news conference.
"We wanted our experts to be there to observe their work, but not during interviews," he said. "Our experts must be there to observe facts that will be found on the spot."

The government opposed the inclusion of Chilean Roberto Garreton, the U.N. special rapporteur for human rights, who has accused Kabila's forces of massacring refugees in the ex-Zaire. The U.N. acquiesced to allow the probe to proceed.
The government also demanded that the probe be extended back to 1993 so as not to just cover its seven-month rebellion that toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May.
"Today Roberto Garreton is no longer part of the commission. We are content that the date had been put back," Mwenze said.

Over a million Hutus crossed into ex-Zaire fearing reprisals for the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of minority Tutsis by Hutu hardliners. The bulk returned home but relief officials say up to 200,000 remain unaccounted for.
